summary: Money cases and life-and-death cases both need careful questioning of the witnesses. But in many ways the court is much more careful in life-and-death cases, always looking for a way to save the person.

chunks.he: אֶחָד דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת וְאֶחָד דִּינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת,
chunks.en: Both money cases and life-and-death cases
chunks.st: Both cases of monetary law and cases of capital law are equal with regard to

chunks.en: need careful questioning of the witnesses,
chunks.st: the requirement for inquiry and interrogation of the witnesses,

chunks.en: as it says,
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: "You shall have one law."
chunks.st: “You shall have one manner of law”
chunks.stMore: (Leviticus 24:22), meaning that all legal procedures must be uniform. Having stated the essential similarity between the two, the mishna enumerates the differences between them.

chunks.he: מַה בֵּין דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת לְדִינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת.
chunks.en: What is the difference between money cases and life-and-death cases?
chunks.st: What are the differences between cases of monetary law and cases of capital law?

chunks.en: Money cases are judged by three,
chunks.st: Cases of monetary law are judged by a court of three judges,

chunks.en: and life-and-death cases by twenty-three.
chunks.st: and cases of capital law are judged by a court of twenty-three judges.

chunks.en: In money cases, the judges may start
chunks.st: In cases of monetary law, the court opens the deliberations

chunks.en: with a reason for "not guilty" or for "guilty."
chunks.st: either with a claim to exempt the accused, or with a claim to find him liable.

chunks.en: In life-and-death cases, they start with a reason for "not guilty,"
chunks.st: And in cases of capital law, the court opens the deliberations with a claim to acquit the accused,

chunks.en: and they do not start with "guilty."
chunks.st: but it does not open the deliberations with a claim to find him liable.

chunks.he: דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת מַטִּין עַל פִּי אֶחָד
chunks.en: In money cases, one extra judge is enough to decide
chunks.st: In cases of monetary law, the court directs, i.e., issues, the ruling based on a majority of one judge,

chunks.en: either "not guilty" or "guilty."
chunks.st: either to exempt, or to find liable.

chunks.he: וְדִינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת מַטִּין עַל פִּי אֶחָד לִזְכוּת
chunks.en: In life-and-death cases, one extra judge is enough for "not guilty,"
chunks.st: But in cases of capital law, the court directs the judgment based on a majority of one judge to acquit

chunks.en: but for "guilty" you need two extra.
chunks.st: and based on a majority of two judges to find liable.

chunks.en: In money cases, they may open the case again
chunks.st: In cases of monetary law, the court brings the accused back to be judged again if new evidence arises,

chunks.en: for "not guilty" or for "guilty."
chunks.st: either with a claim to exempt the accused, or with a claim to find him liable.

chunks.en: In life-and-death cases, they open it again for "not guilty,"
chunks.st: In cases of capital law, the court brings the accused back to be judged again with a claim to acquit him,

chunks.en: but not for "guilty."
chunks.st: but the court does not bring him back to be judged with a claim to find him liable.

chunks.he: דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת הַכֹּל מְלַמְּדִין זְכוּת וְחוֹבָה,
chunks.en: In money cases, everyone may give a reason for "not guilty" or "guilty."
chunks.st: In cases of monetary law, all those present at the trial may teach a reason to exempt a litigant or to find him liable.

chunks.en: In life-and-death cases, everyone may give a reason for "not guilty,"
chunks.st: In cases of capital law, all those present at the trial may teach a reason to acquit the accused,

chunks.en: but not everyone may give a reason for "guilty."
chunks.st: but not all present may teach a reason to find him liable.
chunks.stMore: Only the judges can teach a reason to find him liable.

chunks.he: דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת הַמְלַמֵּד חוֹבָה מְלַמֵּד זְכוּת
chunks.en: In money cases, a judge who gave a reason for "guilty" may give one for "not guilty,"
chunks.st: In cases of monetary law, one who initially teaches a reason to find the accused liable may then teach a reason to exempt him,

chunks.en: and one who gave a reason for "not guilty" may give one for "guilty."
chunks.st: and one who initially teaches a reason to exempt him may then teach a reason to find him liable.

chunks.he: דִּינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת הַמְלַמֵּד חוֹבָה מְלַמֵּד זְכוּת,
chunks.en: In life-and-death cases, one who said "guilty" may switch to "not guilty,"
chunks.st: In cases of capital law, one who initially teaches a reason to find him liable may then teach a reason to acquit,

chunks.en: but one who said "not guilty"
chunks.st: but one who initially teaches a reason to acquit

chunks.en: may not switch back to "guilty."
chunks.st: may not return and teach a reason to find him liable.

chunks.he: דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת דָּנִין בַּיּוֹם וְגוֹמְרִין בַּלַּיְלָה,
chunks.en: Money cases are judged in the day, and may be finished at night.
chunks.st: In cases of monetary law, the court judges during the daytime, and may conclude the deliberations and issue the ruling even at night.

chunks.he: דִּינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת דָּנִין בַּיּוֹם וְגוֹמְרִין בַּיּוֹם.
chunks.en: Life-and-death cases are judged in the day, and finished in the day.
chunks.st: In cases of capital law, the court judges during the daytime, and concludes the deliberations and issues the ruling only in the daytime.

chunks.en: Money cases may be finished on the same day,
chunks.st: In cases of monetary law, the court may conclude the deliberations and issue the ruling even on that same day,

chunks.en: whether for "not guilty" or for "guilty."
chunks.st: whether to exempt the accused or to find him liable.

chunks.he: דִּינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת גּוֹמְרִין בּוֹ בַיּוֹם לִזְכוּת
chunks.en: Life-and-death cases may be finished on the same day for "not guilty,"
chunks.st: In cases of capital law, the court may conclude the deliberations and issue the ruling even on that same day to acquit the accused,

chunks.en: but only on the next day for "guilty."
chunks.st: but must wait until the following day to find him liable.

chunks.en: So we do not judge them
chunks.st: Therefore, since capital cases might continue for two days, the court does not judge cases of capital law on certain days,

chunks.en: not on Erev Shabbos,
chunks.st: neither on the eve of Shabbat

chunks.en: and not on Erev Yom Tov.
chunks.explain: The case might need a second day, which would be Shabbos or Yom Tov.
chunks.st: nor the eve of a Festival.

summary: This mishnah teaches which judge speaks first in different cases, and who may be a judge in life-and-death cases.

chunks.he: דִּינֵי הַטֻּמְאוֹת וְהַטָּהֳרוֹת מַתְחִילִין מִן הַגָּדוֹל,
chunks.en: In cases of tumah and taharah, the judges start with the greatest judge.
chunks.st: In cases of monetary law, and likewise in the cases of ritual impurity and purity, the judges commence expressing their opinions from the greatest of the judges.

words.note: Halachos of what is tamei and tahor.

chunks.en: In life-and-death cases, they start from the side.
chunks.explain: The smaller judges speak first, so they are not afraid to disagree with the great ones.
chunks.st: In cases of capital law, the judges commence issuing their opinions from the side, where the least significant judges sit.

chunks.en: Everyone may judge money cases,
chunks.st: All are fit to judge cases of monetary law.

chunks.he: וְאֵין הַכֹּל כְּשֵׁרִין לָדוּן דִּינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת,
chunks.en: but not everyone may judge life-and-death cases,
chunks.st: But not all are fit to judge cases of capital law;

chunks.en: only Kohanim, Levi'im,
chunks.st: only priests, Levites,

chunks.en: and Yisraelim whose daughters may marry Kohanim.
chunks.explain: Families with a clean, proper yichus.
chunks.st: and Israelites who are of sufficiently fit lineage to marry their daughters to members of the priesthood are fit to judge cases of capital law.

summary: The Sanhedrin sat in a half circle so all the judges could see each other. Scribes wrote down what each judge said.

chunks.en: The Sanhedrin sat like half of a round threshing floor,
chunks.st: A Sanhedrin of twenty-three was arranged in the same layout as half of a circular threshing floor,

words.note: A flat place where grain is threshed.

chunks.he: כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהוּ רוֹאִין זֶה אֶת זֶה.
chunks.en: so that they could see one another.
chunks.st: in order that all the judges will see one another and the witnesses.

chunks.en: And two scribes of the judges stand in front of them,
chunks.st: And two judges’ scribes stand before the court,

chunks.en: one on the right and one on the left,
chunks.st: one on the right and one on the left,

chunks.en: and they write the words of those who say "not guilty" and those who say "guilty."
chunks.st: and they write the statements of those who find the accused liable and the statements of those who acquit the accused.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says, three.
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says: There were three scribes.

chunks.en: One writes the words of those who say "not guilty,"
chunks.st: One writes only the statements of those who acquit the accused,

chunks.en: and one writes the words of those who say "guilty,"
chunks.st: one writes only the statements of those who find him liable,

chunks.he: וְהַשְּׁלִישִׁי כוֹתֵב דִּבְרֵי הַמְזַכִּין וְדִבְרֵי הַמְחַיְּבִין:
chunks.en: and the third writes both.
chunks.st: and the third writes both the statements of those who acquit the accused and the statements of those who find him liable,
chunks.stMore: so that if there is uncertainty concerning the precise wording that one of the scribes writes, it can be compared to the words of the third scribe.

summary: Three rows of talmidei chachamim sat in front of the Sanhedrin. When a new judge was needed, they took him from the first row, and everyone moved up.

chunks.en: And three rows of talmidei chachamim
chunks.st: And three rows of Torah scholars

chunks.en: sit in front of them,
chunks.st: sit before the judges, and

chunks.he: כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד מַכִּיר אֶת מְקוֹמוֹ.
chunks.en: each one knows his place.
chunks.st: each and every one among those sitting recognizes his place,
chunks.stMore: i.e., they are seated in accordance with their stature.

chunks.en: If they needed to give semichah to a new judge,
chunks.st: When the court must ordain
chunks.stMore: an additional judge, e.g., if a judge dies during the proceedings or in the case of a court without a decisive majority (see 40a), the court

chunks.en: they took him from the first row.
chunks.st: ordains the greatest Torah scholar from the first row.

chunks.he: אֶחָד מִן הַשְּׁנִיָּה בָּא לוֹ לָרִאשׁוֹנָה
chunks.en: One from the second row moves to the first,
chunks.st: As a seat in the first row is now vacant, one Torah scholar from the second row comes to the first row,

chunks.he: וְאֶחָד מִן הַשְּׁלִישִׁית בָּא לוֹ לַשְּׁנִיָּה,
chunks.en: and one from the third row moves to the second,
chunks.st: and one Torah scholar from the third row comes to the second row,

chunks.he: וּבוֹרְרִין לָהֶן עוֹד אֶחָד מִן הַקָּהָל
chunks.en: and they choose one more from the crowd
chunks.st: and the court selects another Torah scholar from among the assembled

chunks.en: and seat him in the third row.
chunks.st: and they seat him in the third row.

chunks.he: וְלֹא הָיָה יוֹשֵׁב בִּמְקוֹמוֹ שֶׁל רִאשׁוֹן,
chunks.en: He would not sit in the seat of the first one,
chunks.st: And this Torah scholar who moves from the second row to the first row would not sit in the place of the first Torah scholar, who joined the court,

chunks.en: but he sits in the place that fits him.
chunks.st: rather, he would sit in the place appropriate for him,
chunks.stMore: i.e., at the end of that row, in accordance with his stature.

summary: Before witnesses testify in a life-and-death case, the judges warn them how serious it is. Every person is like a whole world, because Hashem created Adam alone, and each person must say, "The world was created for me."

chunks.en: How do they warn the witnesses
chunks.st: How does the court intimidate the witnesses in giving

chunks.en: in life-and-death cases?
chunks.st: testimony for cases of capital law?

chunks.en: They would bring them in and warn them:
chunks.st: They would bring the witnesses in and intimidate them by saying to them:

chunks.en: "Maybe you are saying it from a guess,
chunks.st: Perhaps what you say in your testimony is based on conjecture,

chunks.en: or from a rumor, or from one witness who heard from another,
chunks.st: or perhaps it is based on a rumor, perhaps it is testimony based on hearsay,
chunks.stMore: e.g., you heard a witness testify to this in a different court,

chunks.en: or 'We heard it from a trusted person.'
chunks.st: or perhaps it is based on the statement of a trusted person.

chunks.en: Or maybe you do not know
chunks.st: Perhaps you do not know

chunks.en: that in the end we will check you with careful questions.
chunks.st: that ultimately we examine you with inquiry and interrogation,
chunks.stMore: and if you are lying, your lie will be discovered.

chunks.en: You should know
chunks.st: The court tells them: You should know that

chunks.en: that life-and-death cases are not like money cases.
chunks.st: cases of capital law are not like cases of monetary law.

chunks.en: In money cases,
chunks.st: In cases of monetary law,

chunks.en: a person pays money and he is forgiven.
chunks.explain: If he lied, he can pay back and be forgiven.
chunks.st: a person who testifies falsely, causing money to be given to the wrong party, can give the money to the proper owner and his sin is atoned for.

chunks.en: In life-and-death cases,
chunks.st: In cases of capital law, if one testifies falsely,

chunks.en: the blood of the person and of all his children who would have been born are on him
chunks.st: the blood of the accused and the blood of his offspring that he did not merit to produce are ascribed to the witness’s testimony

chunks.en: until the end of the world.
chunks.st: until eternity.

chunks.he: שֶׁכֵּן מָצִינוּ בְקַיִן שֶׁהָרַג אֶת אָחִיו,
chunks.en: That is what we find with Kayin, who killed his brother,
chunks.st: The proof for this is as we found with Cain, who killed his brother,

chunks.en: as it says, 'The bloods of your brother cry out.'
chunks.st: as it is stated concerning him: “The voice of your brother’s blood [demei] cries out to Me from the ground” (Genesis 4:10).

chunks.en: It does not say 'the blood of your brother,'
chunks.st: The verse does not state: Your brother’s blood [dam], in the singular,

chunks.en: but 'the bloods of your brother':
chunks.st: but rather: “Your brother’s blood [demei],” in the plural.

chunks.en: his blood and the blood of his children.
chunks.st: This serves to teach that the loss of both his brother’s blood and the blood of his brother’s offspring are ascribed to Cain.

chunks.en: Another explanation:
chunks.st: The mishna notes: Alternatively,

chunks.en: 'the bloods of your brother'
chunks.st: the phrase “your brother’s blood [demei],” written in the plural,

chunks.en: means that his blood was spilled
chunks.st: teaches that that his blood was not gathered in one place but was

chunks.en: on the trees and on the stones.
chunks.st: splattered on the trees and on the stones.

chunks.en: That is why Adam was created alone,
chunks.st: The court tells the witnesses: Therefore, Adam the first man was created alone,

chunks.he: לְלַמֶּדְךָ, שֶׁכָּל הַמְאַבֵּד נֶפֶשׁ אַחַת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל,
chunks.en: to teach you that anyone who destroys one Jewish life,
chunks.st: to teach you that with regard to anyone who destroys one soul from the Jewish people, i.e., kills one Jew,

chunks.en: the Torah counts it for him
chunks.st: the verse ascribes him blame

chunks.en: as if he destroyed a whole world.
chunks.st: as if he destroyed an entire world,
chunks.stMore: as Adam was one person, from whom the population of an entire world came forth.

chunks.en: And anyone who saves one Jewish life,
chunks.st: And conversely, anyone who sustains one soul from the Jewish people,

chunks.en: the Torah counts it for him
chunks.st: the verse ascribes him credit

chunks.en: as if he saved a whole world.
chunks.st: as if he sustained an entire world.
chunks.stMore: The mishna cites another reason Adam the first man was created alone:

chunks.en: And it was also for peace among people,
chunks.st: And this was done due to the importance of maintaining peace among people,

chunks.en: so that no person can say to his friend,
chunks.st: so that one person will not say to another:

chunks.en: 'My father is greater than your father.'
chunks.explain: Everyone comes from the same first father, Adam.
chunks.st: My father, i.e., progenitor, is greater than your father.

chunks.en: And so that the heretics will not say,
chunks.st: And it was also so that the heretics who believe in multiple gods

chunks.en: 'There are many powers in Heaven.'
chunks.st: will not say: There are many authorities in Heaven, and each created a different person.

chunks.he: וּלְהַגִּיד גְּדֻלָּתוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
chunks.en: And to tell the greatness of Hashem:
chunks.st: And this serves to tell of the greatness of the Holy One, Blessed be He,

chunks.he: שֶׁאָדָם טוֹבֵעַ כַּמָּה מַטְבְּעוֹת בְּחוֹתָם אֶחָד
chunks.en: a person stamps many coins with one stamp,
chunks.st: as when a person stamps several coins with one seal,

chunks.en: and they all look the same.
chunks.st: they are all similar to each other.

chunks.he: וּמֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
chunks.en: But the King of kings, Hashem,
chunks.st: But the supreme King of kings, the Holy One, Blessed be He,

chunks.he: טָבַע כָּל אָדָם בְּחוֹתָמוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן
chunks.en: stamped every person with the stamp of Adam HaRishon,
chunks.st: stamped all people with the seal of Adam the first man, as all of them are his offspring,

chunks.en: and not one of them looks like another.
chunks.st: and not one of them is similar to another.

chunks.he: לְפִיכָךְ כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד חַיָּב לוֹמַר,
chunks.en: So each and every person must say,
chunks.st: Therefore, since all humanity descends from one person, each and every person is obligated to say:

chunks.en: 'The world was created for me.'
chunks.explain: So I must act in a way that is worthy of it.
chunks.st: The world was created for me,
chunks.stMore: as one person can be the source of all humanity, and recognize the significance of his actions.

chunks.he: וְשֶׁמָּא תֹאמְרוּ מַה לָּנוּ וְלַצָּרָה הַזֹּאת,
chunks.en: And maybe you will say, 'Why do we need this trouble?'
chunks.st: The court says to the witnesses: And perhaps you will say: Why would we want this trouble?
chunks.stMore: Perhaps it would be better not to testify at all.

chunks.en: But it already says,
chunks.st: But be aware, as is it not already stated:

chunks.he: וְהוּא עֵד אוֹ רָאָה אוֹ יָדָע
chunks.en: 'And he is a witness, or he saw, or he knew,
chunks.st: “And he being a witness, whether he has seen or known,

chunks.en: if he does not tell...'
chunks.explain: It is a sin not to testify.
chunks.st: if he does not utter it,
chunks.stMore: then he shall bear his iniquity” (Leviticus 5:1)? It is a transgression not to testify when one can do so.

chunks.en: And maybe you will say, 'Why should we
chunks.st: And perhaps you will say: Why would we want

chunks.en: be blamed for this man's blood?'
chunks.st: to be responsible for the blood of this person?

chunks.en: But it already says,
chunks.st: But be aware, as is it not already stated:

chunks.en: 'When the wicked are lost, there is joyful song.'"
chunks.st: “When the wicked perish, there is song” (Proverbs 11:10)?
